claim: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has one of the worst prognoses among all human malignancies.
source: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has one of the worst prognoses among all human malignancies (Siegel et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Siegel et al., 2016

claim: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are a subpopulation of cancer cells capable of self-renewing and producing progeny cells that are critical for cancer growth.
source: Recently, cancer stem cells (CSCs) have been considered as a subpopulation of cancer cells capable of self-renewing and producing progeny cells that are critical for cancer growth (Al-Hajj et al., 2003; Bonnet and Dick, 1997; Lapidot et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to Al-Hajj et al., 2003; Bonnet and Dick, 1997; Lapidot et al., 1994

claim: Dclk1 is expressed by a small subset of PanIN and PDAC cells.
source: Dclk1 is expressed by a small subset of PanIN and PDAC cells (Bailey et al., 2014; Delgiorno et al., 2014; Ito et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bailey et al., 2014; Delgiorno et al., 2014; Ito et al., 2016

claim: Dclk1+ cells in the normal pancreas harbor the potential function to initiate premalignant lesions when the oncogenic Kras mutation is introduced together with inflammatory stimuli such as caerulein-induced pancreatitis in vivo.
source: Dclk1+ cells in the normal pancreas harbor the potential function to initiate premalignant lesions when the oncogenic Kras mutation is introduced together with inflammatory stimuli such as caerulein-induced pancreatitis in vivo (Westphalen et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Westphalen et al., 2016

claim: Acetylated tubulin+/DCLK1+ PDAC cells have spheroid-forming capacity in vitro.
source: Another group showed a spheroid-forming capacity of acetylated tubulin+/DCLK1+ PDAC cells in vitro (Bailey et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bailey et al., 2014

claim: No longitudinal in vivo tracking of progeny of pancreatic tumor/CSCs for the maintenance of PDAC and its preinvasive precursor lesions has been reported.
source: However, so far, no longitudinal in vivo tracking of progeny of pancreatic tumor/CSCs for the maintenance of PDAC and its preinvasive precursor lesions has been reported in part due to technical issues.
evidence: Statement about the absence of prior research in the literature

claim: Dclk1+ cells in PanINs of KF mice represent 6.54 ± 1.32% of PanIN cells.
source: We observed Dclk1 expression in a small subset of PanIN cells in KF mice (6.54 ± 1.32%, Figure 1D, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Quantitative data from immunostaining shown in Figure 1D

claim: Dclk1+ cells in PDACs of KPF mice represent 0.173 ± 0.029% of PDAC cells.
source: Dclk1 staining was also detected only in a fraction of PDAC cells in this model (0.173 ± 0.029%, Figure 1G, Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: Quantitative data from immunostaining shown in Figure 1G

claim: DCLK1+ cells in human PDACs represent 0.097 ± 0.026% of PDAC cells.
source: Similar to mouse PDACs, human PDACs displayed DCLK1 expression only in a limited proportion of PDAC cells (0.097 ± 0.026%, Figure 1H, Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: Quantitative data from immunostaining of human PDAC samples shown in Figure 1H

claim: Mouse Dclk1+ PanIN and PDAC cells express CSC markers including Epcam, Cd44, Cd24, and Aldh1a1.
source: We observed colocalization between these CSC markers and Dclk1 in PanIN and PDAC (Figure 1K).
evidence: Immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 1K demonstrating colocalization

claim: The proportion of EGFP+ cells in PanIN cells increased from 5.43 ± 0.84% to 35.4 ± 2.03% at 28 days after tamoxifen injection in DRKF mice.
source: The proportion of EGFP+ cells, indicating a Dclk1+ cells and their descendant cells, in PanIN cells increased from 5.43 ± 0.84% up to 35.4 ± 2.03% (Figure 2G, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Quantitative lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2G

claim: Dclk1+ stem cells supply Dclk1− descendant cells in established PanINs.
source: These data suggested that Dclk1+ stem cells supply Dclk1− descendant cells in established PanINs and maintain these lesions.
evidence: Inference from lineage tracing data showing expansion of EGFP+ cells from Dclk1+ progenitors

claim: Dclk1creERT2-IRES-EGFP mice have no leakiness of Cre expression without tamoxifen administration.
source: Therefore, Dclk1creERT2-IRES-EGFP mice had no leakiness of Cre expression without tamoxifen administration.
evidence: Based on data showing complete consistency between Dclk1 staining and EGFP expression before tamoxifen

claim: GFP+ cells in Dclk1− cells were hardly seen (in less than 0.01% of Dclk1− cell population) in pancreatic epithelium after tamoxifen administration.
source: GFP+ cells in Dclk1− cells were hardly seen (in less than 0.01% of Dclk1− cell population) in pancreatic epithelium of the mice with no gene alteration, with Kras single mutation or with both Kras mutation and p53 deletion on day 1 and day 3 after tamoxifen administration (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: Quantitative data from Figure 3—figure supplement 1B demonstrating specificity of Cre recombination

claim: CreER driven recombination is specific to Dclk1+ cells in Dclk1creERT2-IRES-EGFP mice after tamoxifen treatment.
source: Therefore, we concluded that CreER driven recombination is specific to Dclk1+ cells in Dclk1creERT2-IRES-EGFP mice after tamoxifen treatment.
evidence: Conclusion based on data showing minimal off-target recombination

claim: EGFP+ area in PDAC increased from 0.040 ± 0.005% on day 0 to 54.6 ± 5.12% of Krt19+ PDAC area 14 days after tamoxifen injection in DRKPF mice.
source: EGFP+ area increased from 0.040 ± 0.005% on day 0 before tamoxifen injection to 54.6 ± 5.12% of Krt19+ PDAC area 14 days after tamoxifen injection (Figure 3I, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Quantitative lineage tracing data in PDAC shown in Figure 3I

claim: A small subset of Dclk1+ PDAC cells continuously supply descendant PDAC cells and maintain PDACs.
source: These results clearly demonstrated that a small subset of Dclk1+ PDAC cells continuously supply descendant PDAC cells and maintain also the PDACs that were already established in DRKPF mice.
evidence: Conclusion based on lineage tracing data showing expansion of Dclk1+ cell progeny in PDAC

claim: The proportion of EGFP+ cells in PDAC-derived spheroids increased from 1.05 ± 0.001% to 51.3 ± 0.05% 3 days after 4-OHT administration.
source: The number of EGFP+ cells increased significantly from 1.05 ± 0.001% to 51.3 ± 0.05% 3 days after 4-OHT administration (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D)
evidence: Quantitative data from spheroid culture experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D

claim: Dclk1 is expressed in PDAC stem cells that continuously supply descendant PDAC cells in the 3D-spheroid model.
source: These data further supported our notion that Dclk1 is expressed in PDAC stem cells that continuously supply descendant PDAC cells also in the 3D-spheroid model.
evidence: Inference from spheroid lineage tracing data

claim: Liver tumors were found in 40% of BALB/c-nu mice 8 weeks after splenic injection of PDAC cells from DRKPF spheroids.
source: Eight weeks after splenic injection, liver tumors were found in 40% of BALB/c-nu mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: Experimental data from splenic injection model shown in Figure 4A

claim: The proportion of EGFP+ Dclk1 lineage area in metastatic liver tumors increased from 0.014 ± 0.002% on day 0 to 32.1 ± 6.93% on day 14 after tamoxifen injection.
source: After tamoxifen injection, EGFP+ Dclk1 lineage area started to expand and replaced tomato+ tumor areas, and the proportion of EGFP+ Dclk1 lineage area increased up to 32.1 ± 6.93% on day 14 from 0.014 ± 0.002% on day 0 (Figure 4G and H, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: Quantitative lineage tracing data in metastatic liver tumors shown in Figure 4G and H

claim: Dclk1+ PDAC cells show functional stem cell activity in metastatic liver tumors as well as in primary pancreatic lesions.
source: This striking data indicated that Dclk1+ PDAC cells show a functional stem cell activity even in metastatic liver tumors as well as in primary pancreatic lesions.
evidence: Conclusion based on lineage tracing data in metastatic liver tumors

claim: Almost all PanIN cells expressed EGFP in the same PanIN lesions of the same live DRKF mouse at 10 days after AIW installation.
source: At 10 days after AIW installation and the final tamoxifen injection, almost all PanIN cells expressed EGFP in the same PanIN lesions of the same live DRKF mouse (day 13, Figure 5G).
evidence: Live imaging data shown in Figure 5G

claim: Numerous PDAC cells were EGFP+ in the same live DRKPF mouse at 4 days after the final tamoxifen injection.
source: At 4 days after the final tamoxifen injection, numerous PDAC cells were EGFP+ in the same live mouse (day 7, Figure 5J).
evidence: Live imaging data shown in Figure 5J

claim: Dclk1+ tumor cells supply descendant cells in both established PanIN and PDAC lesions in live mouse.
source: These data clearly demonstrated that Dclk1+ tumor cells supply descendant cells in both established PanIN and PDAC lesions in live mouse.
evidence: Conclusion based on live imaging data

claim: EGFP+ PDAC cells efficiently formed many large spheroids whereas EGFP− PDAC cells formed almost no spheroids.
source: Whereas EGFP– PDAC cells formed almost no spheroids, EGFP+ PDAC cells efficiently formed many large spheroids (Figure 6C–F), indicating that Dclk1+ PDAC cells have a high spheroid-forming potential.
evidence: Experimental data from spheroid formation assay shown in Figure 6C-F

claim: Dclk1+ PDAC cells have a high spheroid-forming potential.
source: Whereas EGFP– PDAC cells formed almost no spheroids, EGFP+ PDAC cells efficiently formed many large spheroids (Figure 6C–F), indicating that Dclk1+ PDAC cells have a high spheroid-forming potential.
evidence: Inference from spheroid formation assay data

claim: Subcutaneous tumors were formed from either 100, 500, or 1000 Dclk1+ PDAC cells in a subset of mice, whereas tumors were never formed even when 10,000 Dclk1− PDAC cells were transplanted.
source: Subcutaneous tumors were formed from either 100, 500, or 1000 Dclk1+ PDAC cells in a subset of mice, whereas tumors were never formed even when 10,000 Dclk1− PDAC cells were transplanted (Figure 6G and H).
evidence: Experimental data from xenotransplantation assay shown in Figure 6G and H

claim: Re-transplanted Dclk1+ cells formed subcutaneous tumors in 60% (3 out of 5) of mice, whereas Dclk1− cells developed no tumors (0 out of 5).
source: Re-transplanted Dclk1+ cells formed subcutaneous tumors in 60% (3 out of 5) of mice, whereas Dclk1− cells developed no tumors (0 out of 5) (Figure 6M).
evidence: Experimental data from serial transplantation assay shown in Figure 6M

claim: Dclk1 marks PDAC stem cells with a tumor-forming ability in vivo.
source: These data further confirmed that Dclk1 marks PDAC stem cells with a tumor-forming ability in vivo.
evidence: Conclusion based on xenotransplantation and serial transplantation data

claim: 4395 genes were differentially expressed between Dclk1+ and Dclk1− PDAC cells (p<0.01; 2171 genes upregulated and 2224 genes downregulated in Dclk1+ PDAC cells).
source: To determine the molecular characteristics of Dclk1+ PDAC cells, we performed microarray analysis on FACS-sorted Dclk1+ and Dclk1− PDAC cells obtained from Dclk1CreERT2-IRES-EGFP/+; Pdx1-Flp; KrasFSF-G12D/+; Trp53frt/frt (DKPF) mice (GSE139167), which revealed 4395 differentially expressed genes (p<0.01; 2171 genes upregulated and 2224 genes downregulated in Dclk1+ PDAC cells; Figure 7A).
evidence: Microarray data shown in Figure 7A

claim: Dclk1+ PDAC cells showed significantly higher expression levels of EMT-associated genes such as Vim, Snai1, Snai2, Twist1, and Twist2.
source: Dclk1+ PDAC cells showed significantly higher expression levels of epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated genes such as Vim, Snai1, Snai2, Twist1, and Twist2 (Mani et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2004; Ansieau et al., 2008), and pancreatic CSC marker Aldh1a1 (Kim et al., 2011; Rasheed et al., 2010), which is consistent with the intimate relationship of CSC characteristics with EMT phenotype (Figure 7A).
evidence: Microarray data shown in Figure 7A with citations to prior literature

claim: Dclk1+ PDAC cells showed significantly higher expression levels of pancreatic CSC marker Aldh1a1.
source: Dclk1+ PDAC cells showed significantly higher expression levels of epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated genes such as Vim, Snai1, Snai2, Twist1, and Twist2 (Mani et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2004; Ansieau et al., 2008), and pancreatic CSC marker Aldh1a1 (Kim et al., 2011; Rasheed et al., 2010), which is consistent with the intimate relationship of CSC characteristics with EMT phenotype (Figure 7A).
evidence: Microarray data shown in Figure 7A with citations to prior literature

claim: Gene set enrichment analysis identified 'Multicancer invasiveness signature', 'Stem cell up', and 'Epithelial mesenchymal transition' as significantly upregulated signatures in Dclk1+ PDAC cells.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) identified 'Multicancer invasiveness signature', 'Stem cell up', and 'Epithelial mesenchymal transition' as significantly upregulated signatures in Dclk1+ PDAC cells (Figure 7B).
evidence: GSEA results shown in Figure 7B

claim: Mouse Dclk1+ PDAC cells possess characteristics of CSC and CSC-related signatures such as EMT, invasiveness, and drug resistance.
source: These results further support our notion that mouse Dclk1+ PDAC cells possess characteristics of CSC and CSC-related signatures such as EMT, invasiveness, and drug resistance as described in the previous reports (Mani et al., 2008; Meirelles et al., 2012; Li et al., 2008).
evidence: Conclusion based on gene expression analysis with citations to prior literature

claim: GSEA revealed the positive enrichment of EMT, invasiveness, and stem cell signatures in DCLK1-high PDACs when compared to DCLK1-low PDACs in human PDAC data sets.
source: GSEA revealed the positive enrichment of EMT, invasiveness, and stem cell signatures in DCLK1-high PDACs when compared to DCLK1-low PDACs (Figure 7C).
evidence: GSEA results from human PDAC data sets shown in Figure 7C

claim: There is a strong correlation of VIM with DCLK1 expression and inverse correlation of CDH1 with DCLK1 in human PDAC data sets.
source: In addition, we observed the strong correlation of VIM, the EMT-associated gene, with DCLK1 expression and inverse correlation of CDH1, associated with epithelial state (Figure 7D).
evidence: Correlation analysis shown in Figure 7D

claim: DCLK1+ PDAC cells harbor the characteristics of potential CSCs in human PDAC as well as in mouse PDAC.
source: These data suggest that DCLK1+ PDAC cells harbor the characteristics of potential CSCs also in human PDAC as well as in mouse PDAC.
evidence: Conclusion based on gene expression analysis of human PDAC data sets

claim: Lineage tracing is one of the most rigorous and robust tools to elucidate the natural activity and behavior of CSCs within their native environment in vivo.
source: Regarding this, lineage tracing is one of the most rigorous and robust tools to elucidate the natural activity and behavior of CSCs within their native environment in vivo, because it can directly visualize the hierarchical structures without affecting microenvironmental factors such as stem cell niche and surrounding immune/stromal cells (Kretzschmar and Watt, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kretzschmar and Watt, 2012

claim: This study provided direct functional evidence for the stem cell activity of Dclk1+ cells in vivo.
source: Thus, we provided direct functional evidence for the stem cell activity of Dclk1+ cells in vivo, revealing the essential roles of Dclk1+ cells in expansion of pancreatic neoplasia in all progressive stages.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's findings based on lineage tracing and live imaging data

claim: Dclk1+ cells play essential roles in expansion of pancreatic neoplasia in all progressive stages.
source: Thus, we provided direct functional evidence for the stem cell activity of Dclk1+ cells in vivo, revealing the essential roles of Dclk1+ cells in expansion of pancreatic neoplasia in all progressive stages.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's findings based on lineage tracing data across PanIN, primary PDAC, and metastatic lesions

claim: PanINs that were positive for Alcian blue and Krt19 staining were developed in KF mice within 3 months of age.
source: PanINs that were positive for Alcian blue and Krt19 staining were developed in KF mice within 3 months of age (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: Histological data shown in Figure 1A-C

claim: PDACs that were strongly positive for Krt19 were developed in KPF mice within 8 weeks of age.
source: In KPF mice, PDACs that were also strongly positive for Krt19 were developed within 8 weeks of age (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: Histological data shown in Figure 1E and F

claim: A relatively large proportion of PanIN and PDAC cells showed positive expression of Epcam, Cd44 and Cd24.
source: In good agreement with previous reports showing that the single expression of Epcam, Cd44 or Cd24 alone is not restricted to CSC in PDAC (Kure et al., 2012), a relatively large proportion of PanIN and PDAC cells showed positive expression of Epcam, Cd44 and Cd24, whereas Aldh1a1 was expressed in a small subset of these cells (Figure 1I–J, Figure 1—source data 4 and 5).
evidence: Quantitative immunostaining data shown in Figure 1I-J with citation to Kure et al., 2012

claim: Aldh1a1 was expressed in a small subset of PanIN and PDAC cells.
source: In good agreement with previous reports showing that the single expression of Epcam, Cd44 or Cd24 alone is not restricted to CSC in PDAC (Kure et al., 2012), a relatively large proportion of PanIN and PDAC cells showed positive expression of Epcam, Cd44 and Cd24, whereas Aldh1a1 was expressed in a small subset of these cells (Figure 1I–J, Figure 1—source data 4 and 5).
evidence: Quantitative immunostaining data shown in Figure 1I-J

claim: Dclk1+ tumor cells harbor the potential stemness in formed PanIN and PDAC.
source: These data suggested that Dclk1+ tumor cells harbor the potential stemness in formed PanIN and PDAC.
evidence: Inference from colocalization of Dclk1 with CSC markers

claim: Among EGFP+ PanIN cells (the lineages of Dclk1+ cells), there were a small subset of Dclk1-expressing cells 28 days after tamoxifen injection.
source: Among EGFP+ PanIN cells (the lineages of Dclk1+ cells), there were a small subset of Dclk1-expressing cells 28 days after tamoxifen injection (Figure 2H).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2H

claim: There were very few Dclk1+ cells within EGFP+ PDAC tumor cells 14 days after tamoxifen injection.
source: There were very few Dclk1+ cells within EGFP+ PDAC tumor cells 14 days after tamoxifen injection (Figure 3J).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3J

claim: Parental Dclk1+ cells were sparsely observed in PDAC-derived spheroids 3 days after 4-OHT administration.
source: The number of EGFP+ cells increased significantly from 1.05 ± 0.001% to 51.3 ± 0.05% 3 days after 4-OHT administration (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D) in which parental Dclk1+ cells were sparsely observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E

claim: Liver metastatic tumors preserved histological features of the primary PDACs.
source: Liver metastatic tumors preserved histological features of the primary PDACs (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Histological comparison shown in Figure 4B and C

claim: There were very few parental Dclk1+ cells within EGFP+ metastatic tumors.
source: We observed that there were very few parental Dclk1+ cells within EGFP+ metastatic tumors, suggesting that most EGFP+ cells were descendant of Dclk1+ cells (Figure 4I).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4I

claim: Most EGFP+ cells in metastatic tumors were descendant of Dclk1+ cells.
source: We observed that there were very few parental Dclk1+ cells within EGFP+ metastatic tumors, suggesting that most EGFP+ cells were descendant of Dclk1+ cells (Figure 4I).
evidence: Inference from immunofluorescence data showing few Dclk1+ cells among many EGFP+ cells

claim: The vast majority of Krt19+ cells of PDAC expressed EGFP after live imaging.
source: Histologically, the vast majority of Krt19+ cells of PDAC expressed EGFP (Figure 5K).
evidence: Histological analysis after live imaging shown in Figure 5K

claim: The subcutaneous tumors displayed similar histological appearance to primary PDAC.
source: The subcutaneous tumors displayed similar histological appearance to primary PDAC (Figure 6I and J), and a very small number of Dclk1+ PDAC cells were observed in those tumors as well as in original PDACs (Figure 6K).
evidence: Histological comparison shown in Figure 6I and J

claim: A very small number of Dclk1+ PDAC cells were observed in subcutaneous tumors as well as in original PDACs.
source: The subcutaneous tumors displayed similar histological appearance to primary PDAC (Figure 6I and J), and a very small number of Dclk1+ PDAC cells were observed in those tumors as well as in original PDACs (Figure 6K).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 6K

claim: Passaged tumors were histologically indistinguishable from primary subcutaneous tumors and original PDACs.
source: Histologically, passaged tumors were also indistinguishable from primary subcutaneous tumors and original PDACs (Figure 6N and O), and a very small number of Dclk1+ tumor cells were observed in those tumors (Figure 6P).
evidence: Histological comparison shown in Figure 6N and O

claim: A very small number of Dclk1+ tumor cells were observed in passaged tumors.
source: Histologically, passaged tumors were also indistinguishable from primary subcutaneous tumors and original PDACs (Figure 6N and O), and a very small number of Dclk1+ tumor cells were observed in those tumors (Figure 6P).
evidence: Immunostaining data shown in Figure 6P

claim: GO terms associated with angiogenesis and EMT were included in top 100 GO terms enriched in Dclk1+ PDAC cells.
source: In the GO enrichment analysis using GO_Biological Process data set, 454 GO terms were enriched in Dclk1+ PDAC cells and GO terms associated with angiogenesis and EMT were included in top 100 GO terms (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: GO enrichment analysis results in Supplementary file 1

claim: Dclk1+ PDAC cells were significantly enriched with 58 pathways in KEGG data set, which included those associated with stemness and drug resistance.
source: In KEGG data set, Dclk1+ PDAC cells were significantly enriched with 58 pathways, which included those associated with stemness and drug resistance (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: KEGG pathway analysis results in Supplementary file 2

claim: GO terms related to angiogenesis were enriched in the DCLK1 high expression group of human PDAC data sets.
source: As in the mouse data, GO terms related to angiogenesis ('angiogenesis' GSE16515, GSE32676, TCGA_PAAD) and pathway related to stemness ('Signaling pathways regulating pluripotency of stem cells' GSE36924) were enriched in the DCLK1 high expression group (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: GO analysis results from human PDAC data sets in Supplementary file 3

claim: Pathway related to stemness was enriched in the DCLK1 high expression group of human PDAC data sets.
source: As in the mouse data, GO terms related to angiogenesis ('angiogenesis' GSE16515, GSE32676, TCGA_PAAD) and pathway related to stemness ('Signaling pathways regulating pluripotency of stem cells' GSE36924) were enriched in the DCLK1 high expression group (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Pathway analysis results from human PDAC data sets in Supplementary file 3

claim: Transplantation assays are performed in the context of non-natural environments that contain different niche factors from those in original tumor sites.
source: However, transplantation assays are performed in the context of non-natural environments that contain different niche factors from those in original tumor sites; the use of immunocompromised mice for transplantation of sorted cell populations adds more complexity and artificiality in the model.
evidence: General knowledge about limitations of transplantation assays

claim: The use of immunocompromised mice for transplantation of sorted cell populations adds complexity and artificiality in the model.
source: However, transplantation assays are performed in the context of non-natural environments that contain different niche factors from those in original tumor sites; the use of immunocompromised mice for transplantation of sorted cell populations adds more complexity and artificiality in the model.
evidence: General knowledge about limitations of transplantation assays

claim: This study established the functional role of Dclk1+ tumor cells for the maintenance and expansion of primary and metastatic PDAC and its precursor lesions in vivo.
source: Our study anew established the functional role of Dclk1+ tumor cells for the maintenance and expansion of primary and metastatic PDAC and its precursor lesions in vivo.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's contribution based on all lineage tracing data

claim: This study successfully described the time course of PanIN/PDAC maintenance and expansion that critically proved the Dclk1+ cells as CSCs within established PDAC and its precursor lesions in live mice.
source: Our study successfully described the time course of PanIN/PDAC maintenance and expansion that critically proved the Dclk1+ cells as CSCs within established PDAC and its precursor lesions in live mice.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's contribution based on live imaging data

claim: Signaling pathways that are involved in metastasis are upregulated in pancreatic CSCs.
source: In this study, we observed EMT associated gene expression signature enriched in Dclk1+ tumor cells in both mouse and human PDACs. This is consistent with previous studies showing that signaling pathways that are involved in metastasis are upregulated in pancreatic CSCs (Mani et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mani et al., 2008

claim: Dclk1+ cells possessed CSC-like potentials not only in mouse PDAC but also in human PDAC.
source: These results strongly suggest that Dclk1+ cells possessed CSC-like potentials not only in mouse PDAC but also in human PDAC.
evidence: Inference from gene expression analysis in both mouse and human PDAC

claim: Selective ablation of LGR5+ colorectal CSCs led to tumor regression, which was followed by tumor regrowth upon treatment cessation.
source: In this respect, recent studies showed that selective ablation of LGR5+ colorectal CSCs led to tumor regression, which was followed by tumor regrowth upon treatment cessation (de Sousa e Melo et al., 2017; Shimokawa et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to de Sousa e Melo et al., 2017; Shimokawa et al., 2017

claim: Targeting Dclk1+ cells can be a novel therapeutic option for PDAC.
source: Therefore, given that combined chemotherapy potentially targeted CSCs in the recent study (Shimokawa et al., 2017), our present study suggests that targeting Dclk1+ cells can be a novel therapeutic option for PDAC, although it might have to be combined with standard chemotherapy for the therapy to be effective for a long period.
evidence: Speculation based on the study's findings and prior literature on CSC targeting

claim: Targeting Dclk1+ cells might have to be combined with standard chemotherapy for the therapy to be effective for a long period.
source: Therefore, given that combined chemotherapy potentially targeted CSCs in the recent study (Shimokawa et al., 2017), our present study suggests that targeting Dclk1+ cells can be a novel therapeutic option for PDAC, although it might have to be combined with standard chemotherapy for the therapy to be effective for a long period.
evidence: Speculation based on prior literature on CSC targeting strategies

claim: This study provided insights into understanding the biology of PDAC and novel therapeutic approaches against this dismal disease.
source: These findings provide insights into understanding the biology of PDAC and novel therapeutic approaches against this dismal disease.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's broader implications

claim: Dclk1+ cells continuously provided progeny cells within pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia, primary and metastatic PDAC, and PDAC-derived spheroids in vivo and in vitro.
source: Using genetic lineage tracing with a dual-recombinase system and live imaging, we showed that Dclk1+ tumor cells continuously provided progeny cells within pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia, primary and metastatic PDAC, and PDAC-derived spheroids in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's main findings based on lineage tracing data across multiple models

claim: Genes associated with CSC and epithelial mesenchymal transition were enriched in mouse Dclk1+ and human DCLK1-high PDAC cells.
source: Furthermore, genes associated with CSC and epithelial mesenchymal transition were enriched in mouse Dclk1+ and human DCLK1-high PDAC cells.
evidence: Summary statement of gene expression analysis findings
